 Taylor Ardrey USA TODAY Nov. 17, 2026, 11:11 a.m. ET Hear this story More than 60,000 vehicles are being recalled by Ford Motor Company due to an electrical system defect that could affect visibility for other drivers on the road.
 The notice posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration notes a software issue with the body control module C, which could raise the risk of a crash.
 The issue impacting certain vehicles "may cause the module to freeze, shutting off certain features such as interior lighting and trailer lights," the agency says.
 Here's what we know about the model included in the recall and what drivers should do next.
 Car recalls: 720K BMW cars recalled with fire risk warning. See impacted models Which model is included in the Ford recall?
 According to the NHTSA, 60,956 units are potentially affected. The model included is:
 2026 Ford Transit
 The recall number is 26C49. The safety recall report says a warning sign of the issue is noticing that the "affected features are inoperative or operating in a degraded state."
 The report delves into the safety risk, "If the trailer tail, position, and reverse lamps do not illuminate, other drivers may have difficulty seeing the trailer."

 Car owners are advised to get their body control module C software updated at no cost. This can be done at the dealership or through an over-the-air update, according to the NHTSA.
 Notification letters were sent out on Nov. 12.
 Ford can be reached at 1-866-436-7332.
